transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-01
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Lara Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Ellen Wu (Redwood), Olivia James (Mariner CTO), Diego Ramos (Head of ML), Priya Shah (Platform Eng), Samir Kaur (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick walkthrough of Optimize recommendations, cost examples for batch sizes, and KV cache hit-rate sensitivity.

[00:00] Lara: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Lara from Redwood, this is Marcus and Ellen with me, we're going to run through Optimize today focused on batching and kv/prefix cache recs — high level then a cost model and pilot next steps
[00:23] Olivia: yeah thanks, we have Diego, Priya and Samir here — we're specifically looking to reduce per-transaction token cost while keeping sub-200ms tail latency for our customer-facing flows
[00:40] Marcus: awesome, that is exactly the tradeoff we usually see, quick question to start: what's your current average prompt + response token count and percent of calls that are chat vs static prompt?
[00:55] Priya: rough numbers: avg prompt 180 tokens, avg response 120 tokens, so about 300 tokens round trip. 70% are chat-like with history, 30% are single-shot NLU requests
[01:12] Marcus: perfect — that tells us batching will help a lot on throughput oriented endpoints and KV cache will help the chat flows where prefix reuse is high
[01:30] Ellen: to set terms, prefix cache here = saving the decoded KV state for repeated prefixes (sessions), KV cache = a more explicit object store that we consult for embeddings/long-context reuse, there is some overlap in what customers call them so we might use KV/prefix interchangeably a bit
[01:48] Diego: quick nit, is Redwood's KV cache the same as the kv cache I've seen in open-source runtimes? we run some internal caching but not production level
[02:05] Marcus: similar conceptually but integrated — we stitch it into the serving runtime so we can bypass recomputation of KV keys and reduce token generation. also Redwood Optimize can suggest TTLs and whether to use full-state caching vs prefix-only; it's workload-dependent
[02:28] Lara: i'll go through the cost model slide — big picture, per-token compute drops with batching, but latency at tail goes up; cache hit-rate multiplies into the cost savings non-linearly
[02:45] [screen share noise, slight stutter]
[02:55] Marcus: example numbers — assume model gpt-like 13b on an H100 equiv node: unbatched avg throughput 12 reqs/sec, batched to 8 token batch size we can get 3x throughput improvement. cost/call goes down ~65% for generation-heavy workloads
[03:20] Priya: 65% sounds high — where is that coming from?
[03:28] Marcus: it's from combined batching plus prefix cache on 70% of calls; if you look at the slide the math splits: baseline tokens-per-call * token cost. With 50% cache hit-rate you save the response generation tokens for that portion of calls; batching reduces kernel overhead by amortizing per-request fixed cost
[03:48] Olivia: what about the user latency — we can't exceed 200ms p95 for auth flows
[03:56] Ellen: so two levers: keep small batch windows for critical routes (burst to dedicated low-latency pool) and aggressive batching for async/backfill routes. Optimize allows per-route policies so you can pin latency-sensitive endpoints to smaller batches and replicate to a low-latency tier
[04:20] Samir: technically how do you set per-route batch sizes? is this in the console or via API?
[04:28] Marcus: both — console presets plus API flags. We also have Autoscaling policies and dynamic routing, e.g., route based on latency SLO or cost budget
[04:40] Diego: can you show an example of the TTLs and hit-rate sensitivity?
[04:46] Marcus: sure, switching slide — here's a sensitivity table: at 20% KV hit-rate savings ~20% cost, at 50% hit-rate savings ~40%, at 80% hit-rate savings >60% but depends on sequence lengths. Also cold-start cache misses and cache warmup should be accounted for
[05:10] [background typing]
[05:18] Priya: our session keys are per-customer so reuse is moderate; average session length 5 turns, many customers have similar prefixes, think 40% reuse across calls
[05:30] Marcus: at 40% you'd expect roughly 30-35% per-token cost improvement with recommended batching profile — but latency trade depends on batch window
[05:43] Olivia: could you give a concrete pilot plan? we need to show economics to finance for Q3 budget
[05:50] Lara: yes — 4-week pilot: week 0 prep and telemetry, week 1 start mirrored traffic to Redwood dedicated pool at small scale, week 2 enable KV cache with conservative TTLs, week 3 tune batch sizes and TTLs, week 4 finalize report and run a p95 latency check and cost delta. We usually provide a cost model spreadsheet for your numbers
[06:15] Diego: last time we tried caching we had cache invalidation issues, how does Redwood recommend TTLs for financial data?
[06:25] Marcus: for sensitive data we don't recommend caching raw PII; instead cache model KV state (hidden tokens) and use short TTLs or session-scoped caches. We'll recommend encryption at rest and KMS integration for cache stores in Private deployments
[06:44] Priya: do you support bringing your own KMS for Private?
[06:48] Ellen: yes — for Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; hosted can integrate via customer-managed keys in many cloud providers; we'll share the security pack link
[06:58] Olivia: ok good. what's the uplift vs openai for this kind of workload?
[07:05] Marcus: depends — if you use a single-host open model you'll have less orchestration. Redwood's value is the Optimize tooling and integrated cache + batching which often yields 30-60% unit cost improvements vs naive self-hosting, and compared to OpenAI API our latency/cost tradeoffs are more configurable in dedicated/private setups
[07:30] Samir: any hard numbers on p95 with cache? if cache hit we might be sub-100ms often?
[07:36] Marcus: yes cache-hit read path is quick — p50 can be <50ms for small responses, p95 depends on your network and route; with dedicated low-latency pool we often reach ~120-160ms p95 for chat-like short responses with cache hits. Uncached generative p95 will be higher
[07:58] Priya: for the pilot can we specify SLOs? like maintain <200ms p95 for auth flows and target 40% cost reduction overall?
[08:06] Lara: yes we can define those as pilot success metrics and have the dedicated pool pinned with failover back to hosted if needed
[08:18] Diego: security/compliance question — we need SOC2 + audit logs + SSO, and for some customers we need data residency in eu-west. anything blocking?
[08:28] Ellen: Redwood supports SOC2, SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs; for data residency we can offer region pinned hosted or Private VPC deployment. We'll attach the security pack and the SOC2 report link
[08:45] Olivia: excellent. more technical: how does prefix cache interact with KV cache when you have long context windows?
[08:53] Marcus: prefix caching saves transformer KV pairs for repeated prefixes, while KV cache can store larger extracted context/state (like embeddings or long-term memory). For long contexts we may shard caches and selectively load portions to keep memory footprint reasonable. Optimize recommends the right granularity after seeing hit-rate and token distribution
[09:18] [brief cross talk: someone drops audio for a second]
[09:30] Priya: what's the onboard effort? how long to get pilot running?
[09:35] Lara: typical pilot is 1-2 weeks to instrument telemetry and mirror traffic; if you want Private on-prem it's more time — usually 4-6 weeks for a full Private install; Dedicated is faster, often within days for small pilots
[09:52] Diego: what telemetry do you need?
[09:55] Marcus: request/response token counts, seq length distribution, per-route p95 latency, and a sample set of session ids to estimate prefix reuse. We usually provide a small script you can drop into your prod mirror to gather these metrics
[10:12] Olivia: can we look at an example cost spreadsheet now?
[10:16] Lara: yeah i have a simplified model on the slide — numbers are illustrative: baseline cost/call $0.012, with batching and 40% cache hit-rate cost/call drops to $0.007, that's ~42% saving. If you increase cache to 60% savings jumps to ~58%
[10:36] Priya: these numbers assume what token price per million?
[10:40] Marcus: in the model we use a proxy compute cost per 1k tokens of $0.0025 for an H100 class profile; your numbers may differ if you use A100 or lower spec instances
[10:51] Samir: for our finance review we need the model with our instance costs — can you make that available?
[10:55] Lara: yes — next step we'll send the spreadsheet and we can run the numbers with your instance costs; Marcus will help map between model sizes and instance families
[11:08] Diego: about failure modes — what happens if batch queue spikes and latency SLO is at risk?
[11:14] Ellen: we have preemption and dynamic routing, i.e., route latency-sensitive requests to a low-latency pool, and the rest to cost-optimized pool; also can set strict batch timeouts so a request is sent after X ms regardless of batch fullness
[11:30] Olivia: for the pilot, do we need to sign an MSA?
[11:33] Lara: for pilots usually a short pilot agreement and an SLA appendix for Dedicated pilots; we can do that in parallel with the security review
[11:42] [screen share: pilot timeline slide]
[11:50] Priya: what about the cold-warm cache transition — any recommendations to warm caches before go-live?
[11:57] Marcus: yes we recommend a warmup pass using historical traffic replay or a background prefetch job for top N prefixes; the Optimize tool can recommend an initial prefetch list based on the telemetry you share
[12:15] Olivia: ok, let's talk about specific routes — our auth flow is high priority, order-processing chat is medium priority, and reconciliation jobs are low. How would you map them?
[12:25] Marcus: auth => low-latency dedicated, small batches, no long TTLs; order chat => enable prefix cache with moderate TTLs and mid-size batches; reconciliation => aggressive batching, longer TTLs and possibly async processing to maximize cost savings
[12:42] Samir: do you support dynamic TTL by user segment? we have VIP customers where we might prefer lower cost tradeoffs
[12:49] Marcus: yes per-route or per-customer policy possible with Optimize; you can attach policies to headers or route tags
[12:58] Diego: how do you measure ROI at the end of the pilot?
[13:02] Lara: we provide a pilot report: baseline vs pilot cost/call, latencies p50/p95, incurred infra cost, recommended steady-state config and projected annual savings. Also we include an ops checklist for rollout
[13:18] Olivia: great. i'd like to get the security docs now, can you drop the link in the follow-up?
[13:22] Ellen: will do — i'll include SOC2, penetration test summary, and design for KMS/HSM integration
[13:30] Priya: small question: does kv cache persist across restarts in Dedicated? we have autoscaling events
[13:36] Marcus: yes — for Dedicated we can configure persistent cache backends (redis/rocksdb S3 tiering) and we have autoscaling-aware warmup strategies; we'll document recommended backends based on scale
[13:50] [short silence]
[13:57] Lara: any other blockers?
[14:00] Olivia: nothing immediate — will share traffic profile and stakeholder list this week
[14:06] Diego: we'll pick a pilot window next week, hope to start small scope in 2 weeks
[14:12] Lara: perfect — we'll send pricing, security pack, and the cost model spreadsheet and sync early next week for pilot kickoff
[14:20] [wrap up]
[14:22] Lara: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with action items; Marcus will own the KV config doc and Ellen will send security links
[14:30] END
